title: Relational Reality — Mathematical Structuralism × Buddhist Emptiness
content_html:
Relational Reality

Mathematical Structuralism × Buddhist Emptiness (Madhyamaka / Huayan)

Dimension Mathematical Structuralism Buddhist Relational Ontology
Core claim Mathematics is about relations and structures, not intrinsically characterized objects. Phenomena are empty of intrinsic essence (svabhāva); they arise dependently as relations (causes, conditions, conceptual designation).
Ontology Entities are positions in a structure (e.g., “2” is defined by its place in the natural‑number structure). Entities are nodes in Indra’s Net: defined by interdependence; Huayan emphasizes interpenetration of all things.
Epistemology Knowledge targets invariant relations (morphisms, symmetries). Structural realism in science: relations survive theory change. Knowledge recognizes dependent origination; clinging to intrinsic natures is a cognitive error that generates suffering.
Method Abstract formalization: axiomatics, category‑theoretic perspective, invariants. Analytic deconstruction (prasanga) to reveal emptiness; contemplative analysis and ethical practice.
Time & change Structures are typically timeless once specified; dynamics are modeled as structure‑preserving transformations. Impermanence (anitya): relations are processual; identity is constructed and revisable.
Implication for “things” Objects have no essence apart from their relational role. Objects have no essence apart from their dependent arising* and conceptual designation.
Potential convergence Structural realism: physics reveals mathematical relations, not “substances.” Madhyamaka: phenomena lack inherent nature; reality is a web of dependencies—resonant with structural views.
Key risk Do structures exist without relata? (Problem of “structure‑only” ontology.) Misread as nihilism; requires the “two truths” doctrine (conventional vs. ultimate) to avoid collapse of meaning.

Design Cues

Substrate → Emergence → Experience: Implement data as relations (graphs, adjacency, transforms) rather than fixed “objects.”

Relational rendering: Visualize edges/weights first; let “objects” appear as emergent clusters of relations.

Two truths UI: Toggle between conventional view (objects) and ultimate view (relation network).

Indra’s Net mode: Show mutual reflection/interpenetration (e.g., shader that echoes patches across the graph).
